problem:
The standard matrix $T$ of a linear transformation $T$ and the vector $b\in {R}^{3}$ are given below. Determine if there exists a vector $x\in {R}^{3}$ such that $T(x)=b.$
In the affirmative case, find the value of $2{x}_{1}+{x}_{2},$ where ${x}_{1},{x}_{2},{x}_{3}$ are the components of $x.$  

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 3 \\ 1 & 1 & 1 \\ 5 & 7 & 9\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 3 \\ 17\end{aligned}]
$$

activity_context.topic_title: The Image and Rank of a Linear Transformation

feedback.problem: If $T=[\begin{aligned}3 & -2 & 1 \\ -6 & 5 & -2 \\ 12 & -8 & 4\end{aligned}]$ is the standard matrix of the linear transformation $T$, then $\text{rank}(T)=$
feedback.worked_solution:
Recall that $\text{rank}(T)=\text{dim}(\text{Im}(T))=\text{rank}(T).$ 

So, we need to find the rank of the matrix $T.$ We reduce $T$ to row echelon form, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}T & =[\begin{aligned}3 & -2 & 1 \\ -6 & 5 & -2 \\ 12 & -8 & 4\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+2{R}_{1} \\ {R}_{3}:={R}_{3}-4{R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}3 & -2 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, since $T$ has $2$ pivot columns, we have that 

$$
\text{rank}(T)=\text{rank}(T)=2.
$$
